subject: arcticOutpost
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: arctic research outpost.
Style: Firewatch flat colour.

spec.name: Polar Outpost Seven
spec.description: A Firewatch-style diorama of an arctic research outpost: a red-sided stilted hab with a glowing porch, a teal lab annex with a radome joined by a corridor, a radio mast and generator shed, and a yard of sleds, drums and a snowmobile. It stands on a cut-away snow slab in front of layered sunset ridges and a big low sun.
spec.layout:
STATIC DIORAMA, no joints. A 10 x 9 m snow slab (x -5..5, z -4.5..4.5) with its top surface at groundTop y = 0.5. The slab's cut edge shows strata. The tallest thing is the radio mast (6.2 m, back-left). The sun sits low behind the back ridges.

FRONT (+Z) TO BACK: stairs and path, then the hab porch at z ~1.7 and the hab body (z -2.3..1.3). Behind the hab are the mast, the stacked ridges and the sun.
LEFT SIDE (+X) is the viewer's right. The corridor runs from the hab to the teal lab (x 2.2..4.6, z -2.2..0.4) with a radome on its roof. The front yard (sled, snowmobile, drums, weather screen, flag) is in front of the lab at x 1.4..4.8, z 0.8..4.4.
RIGHT SIDE (-X) is the viewer's left. The generator shed stands at x -4.8..-3.5 and the lattice mast at x -4.1, z -3.0.

Buildings are raised on short dark-wood stilts. Hab floor and corridor floor are at y 1.1; the lab floor is also 1.1. All buildings sink 0.05 into the ground.

STYLE (Firewatch flat colour), applied by every part:
- Every surface is one flat colour with a faceted, low-poly look and no outlines. Forms are big and simple: chunky boxes, simple pitched roofs, few segments (6-8 sides on cylinders).
- The sun is low and warm, coming from +X and a little +Z. LIT faces are the top, +X and +Z faces. SHADED faces are the -X and -Z faces.
- A shaded face is not darker grey. It is covered by a thin 0.02 m shade slab hugging the whole -X (and -Z) face in the paired shade colour: wallRed -> accentRed, trimCream -> snowMid, tealPanel -> deepTeal, wood -> darkWood, radomeWhite -> snowShade, metal -> ridgeNear, roofDark -> ink, snowLit -> snowShade (and snowDeep for the deepest crevices).
- Cast shadows are flat, thin slabs (0.01 thick) in snowShade lying on the ground. They fall toward -X and a little toward -Z, about 1.2 m long. Each part lays its own shadows at its own height: hab y=0.506, lab y=0.508, mast/shed y=0.510, yard y=0.512 (terrain surface is y=0.5, packed path 0.503), so they never z-fight.
- Windows and lanterns are the glow accent: windowGlow and yellow parts, with glow() applied. Snow caps are lumpy snowLit slabs with a scalloped lip, snowShade underneath. Icicles are tiny iceBlue cones.
- Colour is warm on top and cool below. The ridge backdrop is a Firewatch gradient made of three layers (peach far, mauve mid, indigo near).

parts.builds:
The diorama base and scenery behind and around the buildings.
1) SLAB: x -5..5, z -4.5..4.5, y 0..0.5, shown as cut-away strata. Bottom 0..0.18 is rock, 0.18..0.38 is iceBlue with a few wavy snowMid seams, and the top 0.38..0.5 is a snowLit cap whose edge lip is scalloped with overhanging lumps. The front and sides are visible, so give the strata faceted wavy steps. The slab's top (y=0.5) must be flat under the building footprints, because other parts' bottoms sit at 0.45.
2) SURFACE DETAIL: low faceted snow drifts as flattened lumps (snowLit lit side, snowShade -X side), only in the margins (x beyond +-4.3, z>4.1, and along the left edge). Keep them below y 0.85. Wind-ripple strips in snowMid. Packed-path decals (snowMid, y 0.503) from the stairFoot at [0.4,0.5,3.2] to the front edge at z=4.5, a branch to the yard and a branch toward the lab front at z ~0.9. Footprint dents as small snowShade ovals along the paths. Three small rock clusters (rock, ridgeNear shaded sides, snowLit caps) at about (-4.3, 3.0), (4.6,-2.8) and (-1.8, 4.1).
3) PINES: a stand of 5-6 stylised Firewatch pines in pine with ridgeNear shaded sides, 3 stacked cones each, snow-capped in snowLit, 0.9-1.8 m tall, in the front-left corner around (-4.2, 3.6) and a pair at (4.5,-3.2). Keep them outside other boxes.
4) BACKDROP: three stacked extruded ridge silhouettes spanning x -5..5 as thin plates (0.25 thick, each narrower on top as a jagged mountain skyline with a few snowLit peak caps): far ridge ridgeFar at z=-4.3, peaks up to y=3.4; mid ridge ridgeMid at z=-3.95, peaks up to y=2.6; near ridge ridgeNear at z=-3.65, peaks up to y=1.8. Their bases sink to y 0.45. Add snowShade streaks and a few snowLit caps on the mid and near ridges.
5) SUN: a sunOrange disc radius 1.0 (low-segment cylinder facing +Z) at sunDisc [2.5,2.4,-4.45], with a larger yellow disc radius 1.35 just behind it (z=-4.47). Optionally two thin arc bands of ridgeFar floating behind as haze. The sun must stay behind the far ridge's z (-4.3) and sit partly hidden by it.
No buildings, mast or props: other parts own those.
parts.attaches: Provides groundTop (y=0.5) that every other part sits on, stairFoot where the hab's stairs land (path starts there), and the ridge band at z<=-3.55. Keep the surface within x -4.8..4.8 flat and free of lumps near mastBase, generatorShed, sledCentre, snowmobile and drumCluster.

parts.builds:
The main living cabin, the hero building. BODY x -3.05..1.2, z -2.3..1.3 (walls x -2.9..1.2). Floor deck at y=1.1, walls to y=3.3, pitched roof with ridge along Z at y=4.1 (eave overhang 0.2, eaves to x -3.05 and x 1.4, but keep the porch x<=1.2 and the lab corridor mount clear: the right wall x=1.2 is the corridor start).
CONSTRUCTION: 8 stilt posts (darkWood, 0.18 square) from y 0.45 to 1.1 with cross-bracing X boards (wood), skirt boards (darkWood) between them on the shaded back and left sides. Walls in wallRed (lit faces) with horizontal cream (trimCream) siding lines every ~0.35 m on the lit +Z and +X faces, corner posts trimCream, a trimCream fascia band under the eave and darkWood base band. Shade slabs (accentRed) on the -X and -Z faces. Roof: two planes roofDark with a trimCream bargeboard along the gable edges, a lumpy snowLit snow layer on top of both planes with scalloped lip and snowShade underside plus iceBlue icicles along the front eave. A metal stovepipe (chimney) at (-1.9, 3.7, -1.2) up to y 4.8 with a cap, a thin ink soot ring and a snowLit snow cap.
FRONT (+Z): trimCream door frame at habDoor x=0.4 with a wood door (darkWood panels, a little yellow window, brass-yellow knob), a darkWood nameplate board above it with three small trimCream blocks as a number plate, and a yellow lantern (glow) hung on the porch beam at (1.0, 2.6, 1.6). Two big windows at x -2.0 and x -0.9 (y 1.8..2.8): trimCream frames, windowGlow glass (glow), darkWood mullion cross, interior shade stripe, snowLit sills with snow. Gable window (small round windowGlow) in the front gable at y 3.7.
PORCH: deck x -0.4..1.2, z 1.3..2.1 at y 1.1 (wood planks with darkWood gaps), posts at the front corners holding a small roof shed (roofDark with snow cap) at y 2.9, railings (darkWood) on the +X side and front with a gap at the stairs (x 0..0.8). A firewood stack (wood logs ends in trimCream) at x -0.2..0.0 on the porch, a pair of boots by the door.
STAIRS: darkWood stringers + wood treads, 6 treads from porch edge (z 2.1, y 1.1) down to stairFoot (0.4, 0.5, 3.2), x 0..0.8, with two handrails.
SIDE (+X wall, z -0.6): the corridor opening, a trimCream square frame 0.9 wide x 1.3 high at y 1.1..2.4 where the corridor joins, with a darkWood door flap. -X wall: one windowGlow window and a vent. Back wall: a vent and a roof-edge snow lump.
CAST SHADOW: a flat snowShade slab at y 0.506 on the ground, extending from x -3.05 to -4.3 and z -2.6 to 2.9 as a stretched parallelogram going toward -X/-Z. Also a short shadow under the stairs.
parts.attaches: Stands on groundTop via stilts. Stairs end on stairFoot (0.4,0.5,3.2). The right wall opening at corridorStart (1.2,1.1,-0.6) receives the lab corridor. Roof and walls must not exceed x=-3.05..1.4 so the mast part (x<=-3.2) and lab part (x>=1.2, built above the corridor) stay clear. Porch front at z=2.1 is the max; stairs reach z=3.2.

parts.builds:
The science lab annex, its corridor and radome. All at the hab's right (+X).
CORRIDOR: from corridorStart [1.2,1.1,-0.6] to corridorEnd [2.2,1.1,-0.6], a hexagonal tube 1.1 wide, 1.2 tall (y 1.1..2.3), in tealPanel with deepTeal shade slab on the -Z side, trimCream rings every 0.25 m, one small windowGlow porthole on the +Z side, a short darkWood stilt pair under it, a snowLit snow strip on top. A trimCream collar where it meets the hab wall and the lab wall.
LAB BOX: x 2.2..4.6, z -2.2..0.4, floor y=1.1, walls to y=3.0, flat roof with a very slight pitch plus a snowLit lumpy snow layer with scalloped lip (top y ~3.15). Stilts: six darkWood posts y 0.45..1.1. Walls tealPanel (lit +X, +Z), deepTeal shade slabs on -X and -Z faces, a trimCream band at y 2.8..2.95 and corner posts, ink base band. Front (+Z) face: a wide strip window at y 1.8..2.5 (windowGlow glass with glow(), trimCream frame, darkWood mullions every 0.6), a metal door at x=3.9 with a yellow warning stripe and a small hazard sign (yellow square with an ink bolt shape), a wooden step. +X face: a vent grille (ink slats on metal), a duct in metal, an accentRed fire-extinguisher box. Roof: two metal vents with snow caps, a yellow-capped skylight, a square instrument box (trimCream) with an ink-and-windowGlow indicator.
LADDER: on the front face at x 4.4, metal rungs from y 1.1 to 3.0 with side rails and a safety cage hoop at the top.
RADOME TOWER: a metal 4-leg lattice tower on the roof from y 3.1 to 4.0 at labRoofCentre [3.4,3.0,-0.9], footprint 0.9 square, X-braces, a platform deck (darkWood) at y 4.0 with a railing ring (metal). On it the radome at radomeCentre [3.4,4.6,-0.9]: a faceted sphere radius 0.65 in radomeWhite (lit) with snowShade shade slabs on the -X lower side (a hemisphere of facets built from slightly darker panels), thin ink seam rings and meridian bands as small flat strips seated on the surface, and a yellow beacon cone/bulb (glow) on the top at y ~5.3, a base ring of metal. Dome top at y ~5.3.
CABLES: sagging ink cables with tiny insulator blocks from the tower to the lab roof edge and from the lab to the corridor (thin sweeps).
CAST SHADOW: snowShade slab at y 0.508 from the lab toward -X/-Z about 1.2 m (partly under the corridor/hab edge, but not over x < 1.2 beyond what the hab shadow covers), and a smaller one for the radome tower on the roof (a snowShade parallelogram on the roof snow).
parts.attaches: Corridor starts at the hab's right-wall opening corridorStart [1.2,1.1,-0.6] and ends at the lab's -X wall at corridorEnd [2.2,1.1,-0.6]. Stilts stand on groundTop. The lab front (z=0.4) faces the yard; the yard part starts at z>=0.8 so the ladder and step stay clear. The radome rides labRoofCentre.

parts.builds:
The comms mast and power shed on the left (-X) side behind the hab.
MAST at mastBase [-4.1,0.5,-3.0] up to mastTop [-4.1,6.2,-3.0]: a triangular lattice tower 0.45 wide at the base tapering to 0.2 at the top, made of 3 metal legs (tapering rods) with horizontal ring braces every 0.5 m and X-braces between, ridgeNear shaded legs on the -X side, snowLit caps on the cross-braces in the upper half. A concrete-ish rock footing block with snowLit cap at the base. At y 5.2-5.6 a metal platform with three yellow-ish (yellow) antenna whips of different lengths, a red-white striped aircraft warning light: accentRed ball with glow at the very top (y 6.15) and a small yellow beacon below it. At y 4.6 a satellite dish: a faceted radomeWhite dish (shallow lathe/cone, radius 0.55) tilted ~35 degrees up towards +Z and +X on a metal arm and a feed horn (metal rod with ink tip), shade slab in snowShade on its back. A small trimCream equipment box (with ink lines) bolted on the mast at y 3.0 with a windowGlow status light.
GUY WIRES: three thin ink wires (sweeps, radius ~0.01) from the mast at y 4.5 to ground anchors A1 (-3.4,0.5,-3.4), A2 (-4.85,0.5,-3.4) and A3 (-4.85,0.5,-1.4). The anchors are darkWood stakes with metal eyes and snow mounds. Wires must stay at x <= -3.2 and z <= 1.2, clear of the hab body (x>=-3.05) and the ridges (z>=-3.6).
GENERATOR SHED at generatorShed [-4.15,0.5,0.0]: x -4.8..-3.5, z -0.9..0.9, on 4 darkWood skids, walls y 0.5..1.9 in darkWood (lit faces wood, shade slabs darkWood on -X, -Z), a gable roof with the ridge along Z (roofDark) peaking at y 2.4 with a lumpy snowLit snow cap and iceBlue icicles. Door on the +Z face (wood with trimCream frame, a small windowGlow slit window), a louvred vent (ink slats) on the +X face, an exhaust stack (metal) with a bent cap at the top plus a puff cluster of three snowLit-ish smoke lumps in snowMid, two short cable sweeps (ink) from the shed to the base of the mast, a fuel jerrycan or two (accentRed) by the door, two solar panels (deepTeal cells with trimCream frame and thin ink grid lines) on a metal tilt stand on the roof's lit slope, and a yellow warning label on the door.
CAST SHADOWS: snowShade slabs at y 0.510: mast shadow as a long thin streak going toward -X/-Z (clipped inside x>=-4.9, z>=-3.5), the shed's parallelogram toward -X (clipped to the slab edge x>=-4.95).
parts.attaches: Mast and shed stand on groundTop. mastBase and mastTop are listed in mounts. The shed's +X wall is at x=-3.5, leaving a 0.45 m gap to the hab's eave at x=-3.05. Nothing may reach x > -3.2. The mast's ground anchors lie at z <= -1.4 and inside the slab, and clear of the backdrop ridges (z >= -3.55).

parts.builds:
Everything standing in the open front-right yard x 1.3..4.8, z 0.8..4.4, y up to 2.4. Props are chunky and slightly toy-like. All sit on groundTop. Each prop lays its own snowShade shadow slab at y 0.512 toward -X/-Z (length ~0.8 for small things).
1) SLED at sledCentre [2.1,0.5,2.0]: a long wooden expedition sled 0.7 wide x 1.7 long along Z, with two runners (darkWood, curled up at the front), wood slat deck, cross-bars, lashing ropes (ink thin sweeps), and a load: two crates (trimCream with ink lids / metal corner brackets / small accentRed stencil stripes), a rolled tarp (tealPanel cylinder with deepTeal shade, ink straps) and a yellow jerrycan. Snow caps (snowLit) on the cargo.
2) SNOWMOBILE at snowmobile [3.6,0.5,3.2], heading +Z rotated about 25 degrees toward +X: chunky, 1.0 wide skis (metal) x 1.9 long body with a hood in accentRed (lit)/wallRed shade, a tealPanel stripe, a windscreen (iceBlue, thin), a handlebar (ink) with mirrors, a seat (ink with a trimCream edge), a rear rack with a small box (yellow), track (ink with metal bogie wheels visible), a headlight (windowGlow, glow) and a snow dusting.
3) FUEL DRUMS at drumCluster [4.3,0.5,1.5]: 4 drums (yellow and accentRed, 0.28 radius, 0.6 tall, low-poly cylinders with ink ring ribs and metal lids), two standing and one lying on a darkWood cradle, with a snowLit snow cap on each lit top and a hand pump (metal) on one.
4) WEATHER SCREEN at weatherScreen [2.0,0.5,3.9]: a Stevenson screen, a trimCream louvered box on 4 darkWood legs (1.1 m high), slatted louvres as thin horizontal strips (snowMid shaded), a hinged front door with a tiny knob, plus an anemometer pole (metal, 2.2 m high) at its side with a 3-cup rotor (yellow cups) and a wind vane (accentRed), and a small snow gauge (metal tube with ink tick marks).
5) FLAG at flagPole [4.4,0.5,3.9]: a metal flag pole 2.3 m with a ball finial, an accentRed flag with a trimCream cross/emblem made of small blocks (swept back in the breeze, faceted wavy cloth built from 3 angled segments), a rock cairn base (rock with snowLit caps).
6) EXTRAS: two or three snowy poles with a string of lights between the hab porch side and the lab (if reachable) is NOT allowed outside the box, so use instead a lantern post (darkWood post 1.4 m with a yellow lantern glow) at (1.6, 0.5, 1.0) with a small snowLit cap, and a small signpost (darkWood with two trimCream boards and ink arrow shapes) near the path at (1.5, 0.5, 4.0). Trodden packed snow patches in snowMid around the sled (flat, y 0.504) and two skid tracks leading from the snowmobile toward the front edge.
Nothing may stand on the stair path strip x -0.2..1.0, z 2.1..4.5 except the signpost at x 1.5.
parts.attaches: All props stand on groundTop at the listed mounts. The yard starts at z=0.8, in front of the lab's front face (z=0.4), clearing the ladder and step. Its left edge x=1.3 is clear of the hab porch and stair region (x<=1.2), and the path from stairFoot (0.4,0.5,3.2) passes at x<1.2.

calls.reasoning:
I'm setting up a spec for an arctic research outpost diorama in Firewatch's flat-colour style: a static model with no joints, four to five parts, and an 8 by 4 snow terrain base.

I'm settling the diorama's footprint at roughly 10 by 9 units with a height near 5 to fit an antenna mast, then sketching out the parts. The terrain base covers the snow slab, rocks, drifts and layered mountain silhouettes at the back. The main habitation module is a rectangular, rounded-corner building on stilts, and I'm now beginning to outline a separate lab annex linked by a corridor.

I'm laying out the rest of the outpost: a utilities group with a radio mast, satellite dish, generator shed, fuel tanks and a sled with crates, plus a radar dome on a tower for the annex. I'm fixing the ground at y=0.5 and sinking the other parts slightly into the snow, then placing the main habitation module on stilts with its walls and roof height set.

I'm placing the main hab's door and an entry deck on its front face, with stairs running down to the snow. I'm then sizing the hab's bounding box so it includes those stairs, and turning to the lab annex, which will sit on the opposite side of the hab from the corridor.

I'm placing the utilities group now, starting with a radio mast at the back left of the base, roughly 5.8 units tall. I'm also working out the lab's dimensions and its link to the main hab, which means the corridor belongs to the annex and the hab's footprint ends at the wall. Behind the hab I'm starting to position the generator shed.

I'm working through the terrain base's bounds: a slab running from x -5 to 5 and z -4.5 to 4.5, with the back mountain silhouettes rising above it. Since the mountains only occupy the rear strip, I'm weighing whether one large box can cover the whole terrain piece even though it will overlap the other parts.

I'm sorting out the utilities now, splitting the radio mast and power gear into a separate piece on the left side of the base and keeping the front-right items apart from them. I'm still weighing whether the overlapping boxes are acceptable for the terrain.

I'm working out the mast's position and guy-wire anchors, so the anchors sit outside the hab's footprint while staying inside the base.

I'm now checking the mast's bounding box against the main hab's footprint, which conflicts once the hab is widened, so I'm shifting the hab's left edge to x -3.0 to clear it.

I'm checking the mast's footprint against the main hab, placing its guy-wire anchors behind the hab at z of -2.6 or less so they stay clear of the building's walls and roof overhang.

I'm adding the front yard as a fifth part, a box covering the area in front of the lab, with the sled, snowmobile, drums and flag. I'm also putting the fuel tanks behind the lab, between the lab and the back edge of the base.

I'm placing the yard items next: a snowmobile and sled at the front right, a weather station near the porch, and the fuel tank cradle nearby, with the exact spots still to be set.

I'm placing the snowmobile and sled on the front-right yard, with the fuel drums, weather station and flag set at their own spots around the lab and porch.

I'm settling the lab's stilts and floor heights, with the walls running up to 2.6 and a slightly pitched roof, then adding a radome tower on top that tops out near 5.15. I'm noting the overall height cap at 6.2 and the radome box limit of 5.3 for the lab.

I'm now setting the lab's bounds and aligning its floor with the hab at y 1.1, so the corridor between them sits level. I'm moving the radome tower up from 3.0 to 4.0 with a dome centred at 4.6 that tops out near 5.25.

I'm settling the palette now: warm peach for the lit snow, lavender and deep violet for the shadows, and a burnt red-orange for the hab walls with cream trim and a pale snow roof.

I'm choosing the palette now: a peach-toned snow for lit areas, lavender and violet for shadows, and a few teals and dark pines for the terrain accents.

I'm listing out the palette swatches now, starting with the snow tones, then the ridge layers, rock, wall and trim colours, and roof, window and wood accents, aiming for twelve so far.

I'm finishing the palette and the part budgets, with the joints left empty since the diorama is static. I'm also starting to sketch the layout conventions, with flat colour and simple shapes, and working out how light and shadow fall across the buildings.

I'm settling the lighting convention now: a low sun from the +X side, so lit faces and roofs stay warm while the -X faces fall into lavender and violet shade. Each part will carry its own flat shadow decal on the snow just above the ground, stretching toward -X.

I'm now assigning a separate shadow height to each part, so the terrain sits at 0.500 and the hab, lab, mast and yard decals stack a little above it to avoid flickering where they overlap. I'm also starting to set the ground pad height across the flat zone under the buildings.

I'm sketching the terrain's edges now: drifts and low-poly lumps around the rim, rocks, and tracks, all kept clear of the building footprints. I'm also placing a small cluster of four or five pines at the front-left corner and a ridge backdrop at the back, and I'm wondering whether the base needs a layered ice-edge cross-section.

I'm giving the terrain slab its strata: a snow cap on top with a wavy lip, an ice-blue middle layer, and dark rock at the bottom. I'm also planning a packed-snow footpath from the hab stairs toward the lab and yard, with the stair foot sitting near z 3.2 under the porch.

I'm pinning down the anchor points for the diorama: the ground at the top of the terrain, the main hab's centre and floor, its door and porch, the stair foot in the snow, and where the corridor starts.

I'm listing the yard anchor points: the sled, snowmobile, fuel drums, and weather station, plus the flag and the back fuel tanks, each at its own mount near the lab and porch.

I'm sorting out where the mast's guy-wire anchors go, checking them against the ridge at the back and the hab's back wall, and settling on points that stay clear of both.

I'm working out the mast's guy-wire anchors, dropping the one that would sit in the generator shed and settling on a point toward the left edge instead. I'm also setting the mast's bounding box so it stays clear of the ridge and the hab.

I'm laying out the generator shed as a small dark red-brown gable box, with a door, a vent and an exhaust stack, and I'm keeping its footprint between x -4.8 and -3.5 so it stays clear of the mast. I'm also considering a cable run from the mast, but I'm leaning toward skipping it since it would cross other boxes.

I'm now sizing the diorama at 10 wide, 6.2 tall and 9 deep, and starting to write out the part boxes, beginning with the terrain slab.

Now I'm assigning colours to the far, middle and near ridge layers, with a pinkish-peach for the far ridge and deep purple-teal for the near one, and I'm setting the rock colour separately.

I'm settling on a palette of hex colours and deciding where the sun disc sits: a yellow disc with an orange ring, placed behind the far ridge so the light falls from the +X side.

Still listing the palette: the snow, ridge, rock, wall and trim colours, plus the roof, window, wood and metal accents, all as hex values.

I'm now defining the palette as flat hex values and planning to write the part layout, with a rule that shaded faces use a darker companion colour from the same set.

I'm settling the shading rules: light comes from the +X and +Z sides, so the lit faces are those and the -X and -Z faces take the darker companion colours. I'm also setting the shadow direction toward -X and slightly -Z, which means the hab's shadow falls across to x -3.05.

I'm working out how to shade the walls, settling on a thin darker slab over the -X and -Z faces, since each box only takes one colour. I'm also keeping the sun and halo rings in as they are.

I'm describing the habitation module's finer details: eight dark-wood stilts, red siding with cream trim lines, framed windows with warm glowing glass, and a wooden door with a porch, awning, lantern and boot rack. I'm also adding a snowy roof with icicles, a metal chimney, and a small "07" sign plate.

I'm adding details to the habitation module: a darkwood name plate over the door with cream blocks, stairs with wood treads and railings, and some vent pipes. I'm also weighing where a firewood stack should go on the porch, leaving the exact spot to the hab builder. Then I'm turning to the lab, starting with a hexagonal teal corridor tube with accordion rings and windows.

I'm placing the lab's hexagonal corridor tube, then giving the lab its roof, radome tower and a faceted radome with a yellow beacon. I'm also fitting a ladder and a cable run, and I'm setting the yard and mast details, with the dish angled up at about 35 degrees.

I'm going to write one function that builds the front yard, aiming for something efficient but still detailed. It'll be static with no joints, using b.part for the geometry and colour, with the glow coming from the kit. The Ctx type comes from the module, so I'll destructure the parameter with a loose type and won't import it.

Still writing the box and placement helpers...

I'm sketching out the sled next, placing it at a fixed spot with runners and a front that curls up, with seven slats for the deck.

Still laying out the deck: seven slats running along the width, spaced toward the rear, with a couple of cream crates, a rolled tarp, and a yellow jerrycan on top.

Still placing the snowmobile, rotated about 25 degrees: skis on either side, a rear track with wheels, and a red chassis with a sloped hood up front.

Still placing the snowmobile's details: a shaded side panel, a tilted windscreen, handlebars with mirrors, a seat, and a rear rack with a yellow box strapped on.

Still placing the drums: two standing and one lying on a cradle, spread around the snowmobile's footprint.

Still placing the drums: one lying on a cradle at the back, and standing ones spaced so they don't overlap.

Still placing the drums: a standing one at the back and two more around the snowmobile, with a lying drum on a cradle beside them.

Still placing the drums: the lying one gets a metal rod pump with a small handle, then a darkWood-legged screen at the front, with a cream box panel sitting on top.

Still placing the weather screen's louvres, door, and sloped roof, plus the anemometer pole and its rotor.

Still placing the snow gauge, a metal tube with ticks, and then the cairn with the flagpole and flag segments.

Still placing the lantern post and its darkWood shade, with the yellow glow box up top.
